text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that can understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns they learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites and articles. Users can improve results through prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions. LLMs are very useful for tasks like summarizing texts, answering questions or writing emails. However, they also have limits: they sometimes produce incorrect information, and they cannot truly understand the world like humans do.
